name: Scavenged Orbital Works
effects: +10% ship production quality (flat 0.1 on production quality). Overrides apply without calling the hazard base, so no hazard. Nothing else.
why: Only ship quality, no effect on daily life.

name: Ocean Tears
effects: Class LCAttractorLow: adds weight 10 for luddic_church to the incoming immigrant mix (who arrives, not how many). Base hazard call, but no hazard listed. No stability, growth amount, income or other change; the 'joy' in the description has no code behind it.
why: Only changes the faction mix of immigrants.

name: Domain Artillery Station
effects: If the IndEvo_Enable_Artillery setting is on, places a Domain artillery station entity at the planet on first advance; tooltip says it defends the planet from any hostile forces until disabled (destroyed state flagged in memory, needs an orbital station to restore). No stat changes, hazard 0.
why: An orbital gun platform shooting hostile fleets makes the place a little safer.

name: Edict: Exact Clearances
effects: Senate edict: +20% production quality on all player-owned markets, -30% ship hull output (rounded up) on this planet's industries. Removing it before the minimum time adds Recent Unrest. No other effect.
why: Purely ship production economics.

name: Self-Replicating Minefield
effects: Ground defense x2.5 (DEFENSE_BONUS 2.5, tooltip 'Increases Ground Defence Strength by 150%'). Spawns a mine belt terrain (plus a dust ring) around the planet whose IFF follows the owning faction, so hostile fleets get hit. Hazard 0.
why: Big ground defense boost and a minefield against attackers.

name: Fractured World
effects: +300% hazard (flat 3.0), -100% accessibility, +5 ore and +5 rare ore for mining industries. Planet being eaten by a black hole.
why: Accessibility -100% makes it very remote; the huge hazard is already counted.

name: Abandoned Station
effects: Empty apply and unapply. Only a marker on abandoned stations.
why: Does nothing.

name: Dimensional Turbulence
effects: Plain BaseHazardCondition: adds its hazard from condition_gen_data, which is 5 (+500% hazard). Nothing else.
why: Only hazard, which the mod already counts.

name: Cold
effects: Plain BaseHazardCondition: +25% hazard only.
why: Only hazard.

name: Decivilized Subpopulation
effects: +25% hazard, -2 stability, +market size population growth, adds weight 10 of the 'poor' faction to incoming immigrants. Description: bandits and looters on the fringes.
why: Lawless survivors and bandits at the edges; stability and hazard already counted.

name: Enigma II Economy
effects: Empty apply and unapply in the bytecode. The 'stabilize their economy' description has no effect.
why: Does nothing.

name: Frontier
effects: Empty apply and unapply. The demand changes in the description (more weapons/supplies, less luxury) are not applied by this class.
why: Does nothing in code.

name: High Gravity
effects: +50% hazard, -10% accessibility.
why: Small accessibility loss; the harsh living is the hazard, already counted.

name: Hydroponics Complex
effects: Empty apply and unapply. Only a marker condition.
why: Does nothing.

name: Industrial Polity
effects: Empty apply and unapply. Only a marker condition.
why: Does nothing.

name: Stardust Memory Posable Ship Model Series
effects: Uses vanilla ResourceDepositsCondition, which only changes resource output for known deposit ids and hazard if listed; this id has neither, so it does nothing. Description is placeholder text.
why: No real effect.

name: Large Refugee Population
effects: -1 stability only (ConditionData.STABILITY_REFUGEE_POPULATION = -1). The reduced production in the description is not applied by this class.
why: Only a stability change, already counted.

name: Pre-Collapse Military Base
effects: When the owner has a functional Heavy Industry or Orbital Works here, +25% ship production quality on every market of that faction. Hazard 0. Nothing else; the base itself is described as unusable.
why: Only faction ship quality.

name: Old Space Accelerator
effects: Accessibility +50% / +40% / +30% / +20% at colony size 3 / 4 / 5 / 6+ (formula (8 - size clamped 3..6) x 10). Does not call the hazard base; hazard 0 anyway.
why: Large accessibility boost makes it a better-connected place to live.

name: Luminescent Clouds
effects: +3 volatiles for a functional Mining, Fuel Production volatiles demand x0. Listed hazard is +25% and the tooltip shows it, but apply() never calls the base hazard code, so no hazard is actually applied.
why: Only resource effects; the shown hazard is not applied.

name: Ever-Blooming Forest
effects: While the planet is not polluted: +15% colony income, +5 to +8 population growth (size clamped 3..6, +2), -2 food from Farming. Tourists flock to see the blooms. Hazard 0.
why: A beautiful tourist world that draws people in.

name: Military Virus
effects: +50% hazard, -2 stability, ground defense x0.6, population growth -8 to -14 (-2 x (size clamped 3..6 + 1)), adds 'poor' weight 10 to immigrants, +3 heavy armaments from Heavy Industry or Orbital Works. Residents must take extreme precautions to survive.
why: A lingering bioweapon that weakens defenses and keeps people away.

name: Extreme Viral Contamination
effects: Without decontamination: -10 stability, +200% hazard, -45% accessibility, ground defense x0.25, -45% production quality, fleet size x0.5, -1 output on every industry, population growth -25 x 2^size (colony can shrink). VIC anti-EVC buildings (tier 1-3) reduce these; tier 3 cancels almost all of it.
why: A virus-bombed world whose population is dying; the worst place to live short of a ruin.

name: Under Ground Storage
effects: Only while the FSF faction owns the market: stability raised toward a floor of 5 (bonus up to +10). With Nexerelin enabled also +2000 flat ground defense, +2 (flat) combat fleet size and +2 heavy patrols. Nothing for any other owner.
why: A deep self-sufficient bunker with a large ground defense bonus (FSF only).

name: Crashed Ring Segments
effects: +25% hazard; Population industry gets +3 metals and +3 heavy machinery; tooltip says the Nexus Core restoration costs 90% less and the condition is removed once it is restored.
why: Hazard and production only.

name: Floating City
effects: Stability by altitude stage: Stable 0, Drifting -2, Unstable -5, Critical -12. City thrusters need fuel; on a fuel deficit the city descends and at altitude 0 the colony is destroyed. Tooltip: while high it negates Toxic Atmosphere and High Gravity; at Unstable it shows -50 growth. No direct hazard change.
why: Living on a city that can fall out of the sky if the fuel runs out.

name: Logistics Boneyard
effects: +25% hazard; Population industry gets +4 metals and +2 rare metals. Nothing else.
why: Hazard and production only.

name: Collective Defense
effects: Only for apex_design markets: +1 stability, +50 flat ground defense per faction hostile to Apex (shown in the intel tab, excluding remnant and blade_breakers), and combat fleet size +10% per hostile faction.
why: Strong ground defense that grows with every enemy faction.

name: Closed Door Protocols
effects: Only for sephira_conclave markets: +10 stability, -100 population growth, pirates removed from the immigrant mix, many demands cut (drugs, organs, organics, goods, luxury goods -5 each, plus smaller cuts on food, supplies, fuel, ships, metals, crew, marines, weapons, machinery depending on industries). Description: strangers under deep scrutiny, residents armed, patrols around the clock.
why: A guarded, closed society: safe but suspicious and unwelcoming.

name: Cramped Quarters
effects: TASC station marker. Always: adds and suppresses No Atmosphere, sets a 30% base tariff if none, station hazard and accessibility mods from settings (both 0 by default). Only if the Cramped Quarters setting is on (off by default, icon hidden otherwise): population growth penalty of -25 x 2^(size-2) once size reaches 3 plus station expansions.
why: Station living with limited space; real effect only when the setting is on.

name: Imperial Doctrine
effects: Only for interstellarimperium markets: +2 stability, ground defense x1.25, combat fleet size x1.1, Population demands marines (size-1) and hand weapons (size-2) and supplies marines (size-3), +1 marines on other marine-producing industries; immigrants: Hegemony share halved, +5 independent, +5 Persean. Description: mandatory military service, rigid social structure, state police.
why: A policed, militarized society: safer streets but less freedom.

name: Toxic Algae
effects: +25% hazard, +2 drugs from a functional Light Industry, -2 food from Aquaculture. The algae make toxic psychoactive chemicals turned into narcotics.
why: Toxic water and a local narcotics supply: some fun, some harm, some crime.

name: Panopticon Monitoring
effects: apply() and the tooltip are commented out: the condition changes no stats. It is a flag read elsewhere: rules.csv blocks black-market trade and changes landing text while it is present, and the player's Panopticon node building (separate) gives stability and removes Pather cells. Description: the colony is under constant surveillance.
why: Total surveillance: no smuggling or infiltration, but nothing is private.

name: Metastatic Sensorium
effects: +25% hazard, -1 maximum industries, colony income +5% per point of market size of every non-hostile market within 10 LY. Description: endless business parks, thrill rides and holographic sensory suites, badly maintained by drones.
why: An entertainment and tourism world with flaky upkeep.

name: Volturnian Lobster Pens
effects: +1 Volturnian lobster for a functional aquaculture-tagged industry. Nothing else.
why: Only a small production bonus.

name: Pre-Collapse STC Districts
effects: Ground defense x1.1; if player-owned and the Hyperspace Topography slipstream-detection stage is active, +3 LY slipstream detection; friendly and trade fleets in the system get +1 burn and +350 sensor range.
why: Old traffic-control gear gives a small defense bonus; otherwise logistics only.

name: Magnetar Devastation
effects: +150% hazard, -75% accessibility. Tooltip: a planetary shield would be destroyed by the magnetar's ionized pulses.
why: Very remote; the deadly environment is the hazard, already counted.

name: Overgrown Nanoforge
effects: Adds Pollution to habitable worlds and runs an out-of-control nanoforge structure that keeps spreading, taking structure slots. Each growth rolls random effects from a pool: change stability, hazard, accessibility, ground defense, upkeep, supply, force an industry, spawn hostile fleets, explode when destroyed. Exact numbers come from the growth handler, not this class.
why: A spreading rogue machine that can spawn hostile fleets and explode; pollution is counted separately.

name: No Atmosphere
effects: Plain BaseHazardCondition: +50% hazard only.
why: Only hazard.

name: Luddic Path Cells
effects: -1 stability while the cells are active (not sleeper); the tooltip is the Path cells intel. The terror and sabotage risk lives in the intel and base system, not here.
why: Already counted by Landlordsector.

name: Commissioned Station
effects: +20% accessibility, +1 stability, maximum colony size reduced by at least 2 (set so the station cannot grow past size 4).
why: Better access; the size cap does not change daily life.

name: Engineered Utopia
effects: While the colony has fewer industries than its maximum: -25% hazard, +25% accessibility, +2 food from Farming. Lost if all industry slots are filled. (unapply only clears max industries; hazard and accessibility are cleared in the else branch of apply.)
why: A carefully terraformed pleasant world with better access, kept that way by light industry.

name: Recent Unrest
effects: -N stability, N falling by 1 every 90 days; removed at 0. Lists recent causes in the tooltip.
why: Only a stability change, already counted.

name: Scattered Ruins
effects: Plain BaseHazardCondition with no hazard listed: no effect from this class. Ruins only matter to Tech Mining and salvage, which read the condition elsewhere.
why: No effect on living conditions.

name: Vast Ruins
effects: Plain BaseHazardCondition with no hazard listed: no effect from this class. Ruins only matter to Tech Mining and salvage, which read the condition elsewhere.
why: No effect on living conditions.

name: Cramped Quarters
effects: Population growth -10 at size 4, -20 at size 5, -40 at size 6+. Nothing else. Description: the station has little space.
why: Crowded station living.

name: Legio Entrenchment
effects: Only for Legio Infernalis markets: +1 stability per Legio market, combat fleet size and spawn rate +10% (+20% after $tahlan_triggered, +30% on hard mode), ground defense x(1 + 0.2 per Legio market), capped at x3. Description: population oppressed.
why: Heavily defended but the people are oppressed by a warlord regime.

name: Major Disruption
effects: -5 stability, ground defense x0.5, colony income x0.15. Removed after 180 days. Description: industries and defenses destroyed by a massive attack. (unapply does not remove the income multiplier.)
why: A recently devastated colony with little protection.

name: Thin Atmosphere
effects: Plain BaseHazardCondition: +25% hazard only.
why: Only hazard.

name: Volturnian Lobster Pens
effects: ResourceDepositsCondition: +1 lobster (base 0, modifier +1) for Farming or Aquaculture. No hazard, no immigration change.
why: Only a small production bonus.

name: Anti-Vulpoid Sanctions
effects: -50% accessibility. Nothing else.
why: Sanctions cut the colony off from trade.

name: Divine Fox Cult
effects: Needs Luddic Majority and spare workforce capacity: +1 stability; if player-owned, Luddic Church reputation +1 every 30 days (to Favorable) and Luddic Path +1 every 60 days (to Suspicious).
why: Stability and reputation only.

name: Vulpoid Demand
effects: Hidden condition: adds Vulpoid demand of min(cap, size-3) to Population. Nothing else.
why: Hidden demand bookkeeping.

name: Vulpoid Estate Servants
effects: Workforce with no effect of its own: only counts toward the market's workforce total (its 'old-money aristocracy' requirement is not checked anywhere). NPC-only. The description is about household servants for mansions, but no code backs it.
why: Does nothing in code.

name: Vulpoid Rangers
effects: Workforce: -12.5% hazard while it has workforce capacity (its 'failing pre-Collapse terraforming' requirement is not checked). NPC-only.
why: Only hazard, already counted.

name: Vulpoid Customs Agents
effects: Workforce: +25% colony income while it has workforce capacity. Nothing else.
why: Friendlier, busier spaceport trade; mostly economic.

name: GAIA Cradle
effects: +50% ship production quality ('CAULDRON Nanoforges'). No hazard (apply does not call the base). The description is placeholder text.
why: Only ship quality.

name: Megafauna Attacks
effects: Code only changes stability: -1 if the owner faction id contains sindrian_diktat, -4 for any other owner. No hazard (not in condition_gen_data), no raids, no real attack events. The arcology-destroying lobsters exist only in the description.
why: Giant monsters that wreck arcologies are a real danger to homes, even if the code only models it as unrest.

name: Company Loyalty
effects: Stability +3 under Sindrian Diktat, -5 under any other owner. Bugs: unapply sets a -5 stability modifier instead of removing it, so removing the condition leaves a hidden -5; the tooltip code, if the market has no faction, changes the market to Diktat, sets size 3 and tries to remove a wrong condition id (DE_Patrioticfervor).
why: Only a stability change, which the mod already counts.

name: Titan Lobsters
effects: Does nothing: plain BaseHazardCondition with no hazard entry in condition_gen_data. The lobsters are flavor text only (the description says they stay a sight from space for now).
why: The class has no effect.

name: Cramped Infrastructure
effects: If the LunaLib option GrandColonies_AddPenalty is on and the colony has more visible buildings than the threshold setting, multiplies all upkeep by (1 + per-building setting)^(buildings over limit). Nothing else.
why: Only an upkeep multiplier.

name: Siren Song
effects: Uses the vanilla LCAttractorLow class: adds Luddic Church weight 10 to incoming immigrants. No hazard entry, no stability, no special natives in code despite the description.
why: Only changes who immigrates.

name: Orbital Parade
effects: Stability +1 and colony growth +5 (flat immigration weight) while a museum parade fleet is in orbit.
why: A public spectacle that draws visitors and lifts growth.

name: WorldWonderCondition
effects: Hidden helper (showIcon false). If a functional World Wonder of the same faction is in the star system, gives +1 stability. Nothing else.
why: Living in a system with a World Wonder is mildly attractive; the effect itself is tiny.

name: Edict: Subpopulation Cleansing
effects: Senate edict: stability -(size-1), colony income x0.7, growth -size, runs size x 31 days (one month less with a beta core at the Senate). On completion removes every condition whose name contains 'ubpopulation' (all subpopulations) and adds ceil(size/3) recent unrest. Needs a Senate in the system and Military Presence.
why: A forced purge of part of the population: fear and violence on the streets.

name: Edict: Industrial Incentives
effects: Senate edict: +1 output for all industries on the planet, their upkeep doubled. Minimum runtime before removal without penalty. Nothing else.
why: Purely economic.

name: Diktat Infiltration
effects: Magnetar crisis condition: sets the mining industry's volatiles supply to x0 here and adds that volatiles supply to Sindria's population industry ('Shipments from Umbra'). Nothing else.
why: Only moves volatiles production to another market.

name: Forward Operating Base
effects: Stability +3, accessibility -30%, ground defenses and fleet size calculated as if the colony were 2 sizes larger, +4/+2/+1 light/medium/heavy patrols, industries cannot stay disrupted longer than 30 days, growth stops at size 5, troops take 0.35x ground battle damage.
why: A temporary military base: very well defended but cramped, controlled and without civilian life.

name: Knightless
effects: Class MPC_knightsDownedCondition (id and class names are swapped with MPC_knightsDownedCondition). While valid: fleet size x0.3, accessibility +20%, stability +1. Temporary (days remaining shown).
why: Easier trade, but the military is mostly gone and only militias are left.

name: Commercial Unrest
effects: Temporary: stability -ceil(2 x unrest level), accessibility -(0.5 x unrest level), halved for colonies of size 3 or less. The unrest level comes from the Voidsun arrest crisis script.
why: Traders avoid the colony for a while.

name: Military Overextension
effects: Class MPC_churchOverextensionCondition: fleet size x0.9 while valid. Nothing else.
why: A small fleet-size change only.

name: Floating Continent
effects: Plain BaseHazardCondition: hazard -50%. Nothing else.
why: Only a hazard change, already counted.

name: Perpetual Dust Storm
effects: Hazard +25%, ground defenses x1.5, accessibility -10%.
why: Settlements live underground in the dust, which also makes them hard to invade.

name: Arcology World
effects: Stage for Omega-governed colonies of size 11-12: +1 max industries, accessibility +20%, income x1.25, ground defenses x1.5, fleet size +25%, hazard -25%.
why: Huge modern arcologies with parkland, rich and well defended.

name: Domain Majority
effects: Each industry: -1 drugs demand and +1 to every commodity it supplies. Removes luddic_majority. During a cryosleeper awakening (memory flag $aotd_fix_stab) stability -size.
why: Mostly economic; a skilled Domain-era population with less drug use.

name: Closed Immigration
effects: Adds pirates weight = colony size to incoming immigrants and lowers growth by the colony's stability value.
why: Closed borders slow growth and let criminals move in.

name: Making Of Moloch
effects: Only when owned by the Luddic Path: fleet size x1.3 (tooltip also says Sanctified Cores in fleets). Hidden otherwise.
why: Military only.

name: Dense Atmosphere
effects: Plain BaseHazardCondition: hazard +50%. Nothing else.
why: Only a hazard change, already counted.

name: Production Union
effects: Heavy industries: +1 to every demand and every supply.
why: Purely economic.

name: Food Shortage
effects: Stability minus the food shortage event's impact, x4 reputation for player food sales. Temporary until the food need is met.
why: People are short of food.

name: Trade Disruption
effects: Does nothing: the class is marked unused and apply/unapply are empty (all code commented out).
why: The class has no effect.

name: #Templar Control
effects: Does nothing: the market_conditions.csv row is commented out with # and the class exerelin.campaign.econ.TemplarControl does not exist in Nexerelin's jar.
why: Disabled condition, never loaded.

name: Extreme Tectonic Activtity
effects: Plain BaseHazardCondition: hazard +50%. Nothing else.
why: Only a hazard change, already counted.

name: Hot
effects: Plain BaseHazardCondition: hazard +25%. Nothing else.
why: Only a hazard change, already counted.

name: Cetacean Xenolife
effects: Aquaculture (if present and functional) +1 food; accessibility -25%.
why: A protected ocean world with sapient whale herds: pleasant and remarkable, if a little remote.

name: Territorial Defense Force
effects: If owned by a 'free' faction (dassault_mikoyan, SCY, ORA, shadow_industry, star_federation, brighton): ground defenses x2.5 and stability +1. Any other owner: ground defenses x0.25 and stability -3.
why: A free, armed and prosperous citizenry; the defense bonus depends on who rules.

name: Cartel Activity
effects: Stability -2 unless the colony has the Marzanna cartel base industry (ix_marzanna_base). Nothing else in code.
why: A powerful cartel runs the black market.

name: Automated Killsats
effects: If the colony grows above size 3, it is decivilized at once (DecivTracker.decivilize). No hazard and no stability (apply does not call the parent; the stability penalty is commented out).
why: Orbital weapons will wipe out the colony if it grows; everyone lives under that threat.

name: Encroaching Biofactory
effects: Hazard +75%. Population and Infrastructure demands +size fuel (for orbital burns). Military Base/High Command also produces organs equal to its marine output.
why: A living flesh mass creeps toward settlements and taints the water.

name: Glassed World
effects: Hazard +100%, +1 max industries. About every 20-34 days a random industry is disrupted for 5-16 days. Bug: the picker loops while the chosen industry is functional, so it only picks non-functional ones and spins forever (likely a game freeze) when every industry is functional.
why: Mostly hazard and economy; the recurring industry outages hurt daily life a little.

name: Quarry Lakes
effects: Hazard +50%. Refining needs no ore or transplutonic ore but +2 heavy machinery.
why: Poisoned water and collapsed mine pits make it an unpleasant place to live.

name: Rebel Arsenal
effects: Ground defense industries need no heavy armaments (demand x0); Population and Infrastructure supplies marines equal to 2x its crew output. Bug: unapply uses unmodifyFlat on a mult, so the armaments demand change is never removed.
why: Old weapon stockpiles and many trained marines make local forces stronger.

name: Liminal Gateway
effects: Stability +5, fleet size x4, fleet spawn rate x1.2, ground defenses x2, accessibility bonus x0, hazard x0 (hazard becomes 0). Bug: unapply removes the hazard with unmodifyFlat, so the x0 hazard mult stays after removal.
why: A sealed staging world of an alien-serving cult: heavily defended, cut off and uncanny.

name: Defense Autocomplex
effects: Only when owned by neutrinocorp: ground defenses +25 x colony size (flat).
why: AI drone defenses against invasion, owner-dependent.

name: Reinforced Defenses
effects: Ground defenses x1.25 for 60 days (can be extended), then removes itself.
why: Extra troops in anticipation of an attack.

name: Domain-Era Anti-Asteroid Satellites
effects: Stability +2, accessibility -10%, ground defenses +400 flat and x1.5, suppresses meteor_impacts, adds a hidden suppressor that lowers Luddic Path interest (not for free ports). Satellites attack fleets with transponders off and join battles near the planet; Nexerelin ground battle barrage ability.
why: An armed satellite shield keeps out raiders and meteors.

name: Pre-Collapse Spy Arrays
effects: Stability +1, ground defenses x1.1, friendly or trade fleets in the system get detected range x0.5.
why: A hidden surveillance network built to watch dissidents.

name: Organ Harvesting Operations
effects: Stability -2. Extends BaseHazardCondition but apply does not call it, so no hazard. Nothing else in code.
why: A secret organ harvesting operation on sleepers is a grim thing to live next to.

name: Organized Crime
effects: Stability -1 (ConditionData.STABILITY_ORGANIZED_CRIME). Nothing else in code.
why: Crime bosses and armed citizens.

name: Pollution
effects: Hazard +25% (condition_gen_data) and +10 Luddic Path weight in incoming immigrants.
why: The mod already counts pollution.

name: Ancient Megacities
effects: Growth +(size-2) and +5 Tri-Tachyon weight in incoming immigrants.
why: Large ready-made cities waiting for people; growth is up.

name: Ancient Military Nexus
effects: Ground defenses x1.3 if a functional ground defense building exists; fleet size +25% if a functional patrol/military/command building exists. unapply is empty, so the modifiers stay after removal.
why: Old military infrastructure strengthens the defenses.

name: Local Gravitational Dynamo
effects: Only while the system's Gravitational Dynamo is active: hazard -50% and growth +(size-2), +5 Tri-Tachyon immigrant weight. Inactive: nothing.
why: Abundant beamed power when the dynamo runs; growth up.

name: Rogue AI Core
effects: Stability -1 and +10 Luddic Path weight in incoming immigrants. Tracks days active.
why: An unknown AI is loose nearby and breeds alarming rumors.

name: Widespread Ruins
effects: No hazard entry, so the class adds nothing. Other code uses it: Tech Mining output, salvage and mission targets.
why: Mostly an economic tag for Tech Mining; mild salvage interest.

name: Shipbreaking Center
effects: Does nothing: apply and unapply are empty and nothing else in the API reads the condition.
why: No game effect; a big scrapyard is a little noisy and dirty.

name: Lost Belief
effects: Stability -5, fleet size x0.75, hazard +25%, accessibility x0.75. Removes itself if the owner is not the Luddic Church.
why: A crisis of faith in the Church's leaders.

name: Strange Ruins
effects: Does nothing: plain BaseHazardCondition with no hazard entry.
why: The class has no effect.

name: Centralised manufacturing
effects: Ship production quality +30%.
why: Purely military production.

name: Vice Demand
effects: Does nothing: apply and unapply are empty.
why: No game effect; a strong taste for vice means nightlife and some crime.

name: Vulpoid Farmers
effects: If the Vulpoid workforce requirements are met (inhabited, workforce cap, Vulpoid population), farming (or aquaculture) gets +2 production. Counts one workforce slot.
why: Lush, colorful farmland tended by Vulpoids.

name: Crashed Cryosleeper
effects: Growth +5 x colony size and +10 'sleeper' weight in incoming immigrants. No hazard (apply does not call the parent).
why: Strong population growth from waking sleepers.

name: Rogue HEPHAESTUS
effects: Hazard +50%, ship production quality +50%, Heavy Industry and Orbital Works demand +size marines. Bug: unapply does not call the parent or undo the marine demand, so hazard and marine demand can stay after removal.
why: Hostile terraforming machines roam the surface and attack people.

name: Megafauna Attacks
effects: Only stability in code: -1 if owned by the Sindrian Diktat, -4 otherwise. No hazard (no condition_gen_data entry). The described lobster attacks on arcologies are flavour; nothing spawns.
why: Giant monsters that wreck arcologies make the place dangerous and frightening, beyond the stability hit.

name: Scavenged Orbital Works
effects: +10% ship production quality (flat). Nothing else; does not call the hazard parent.
why: Purely military-industrial.

name: Patriotic Fervor
effects: Stability +3 under the Sindrian Diktat, -5 under any other owner. Bug: unapply sets -5 instead of removing it. Surprise: the tooltip code turns an unowned market into a size-3 Diktat colony and removes the condition when shown.
why: Indoctrination and crackdowns cost some freedom; the stability part is already counted.

name: Unstable Fusion Lamp
effects: +75% hazard rating. Nothing else.
why: Hazard is counted; residents also live in fear of the next blackout or flare.

name: Heated World
effects: Uses vanilla WorldIce, which does nothing (empty apply, hidden icon). The fuel demand in the description is not implemented.
why: No real effect.

name: Edict: Labour Restrictions
effects: Stability +4; every industry -1 output and -1 demand on every commodity. Needs a Senate in the system, not a free port; removing it early causes unrest.
why: Shorter working hours make tenants happier.

name: Edict: Wartime Lockdown
effects: Stability +5, patrol spawn rate x2, fleet size +100%, ground defense x3; all non-military industries x0.3 supply and demand. 1 unrest when it ends (3 if removed early); minimum 62-93 days.
why: Full planetary lockdown: very safe, very unhappy.

name: Edict: Trade Incentives
effects: Player colonies without Commerce: adds an independent Open Market submarket; stability -2.
why: More shopping, small plus.

name: Lawless Subpopulation
effects: Stability -2 base, +2 with a Privateer Base, +2 if not hostile to pirates/evil factions (range -2 to +2). Growth -size (no base, disliked) to +size (base, liked). Adds poor immigrants.
why: A large population of pirates and fugitives means more crime.

name: Sabotage
effects: Temporary IAIIC crisis sabotage, holds one or more of: accessibility -20%, fleet size -30%, or about +2 unrest (kidnappings, protests). Hidden when no sabotage is active.
why: Covert attacks (kidnappings, malware, ambushes) make life a bit less safe.

name: Command Disrupted
effects: IAIIC crisis: fleet size x0.4 while the timer runs; inspections postponed.
why: Military only.

name: Disarmed
effects: IAIIC ceasefire: fleet size x0.25 while the timer runs.
why: Orbital fleet only, no effect on ground life.

name: Accessible Sub-Ice Bedrock
effects: Only -50% hazard (vanilla BaseHazardCondition).
why: Hazard is already counted.

name: Parasitic Spores
effects: Drug demand of Population and Mining set to 0; every industry -1 output; stability raised to at least 5 (adds max(0, 5 - stability)); growth +10 x size factor; player-faction immigrants.
why: Spores make people content and empathic but clumsy.

name: Ancient Religious Landmark
effects: Accessibility +10%, stability +1, growth 20 - 2 x size factor, Luddic Church and Luddic Path immigrants.
why: Pilgrim site that draws visitors and trade.

name: Underground Network
effects: Adds (1 - current hazard) to hazard, so hazard ends at about 100% whatever it was (raises low, cuts high; depends on apply order). Growth -2 x size factor, poor immigrants.
why: Life in sealed tunnels is cramped; the hazard change is counted separately.

name: Military Zone
effects: Only for the FSF faction: Population demand for luxury goods -8, drugs -8, organs -4; Mining drug demand -8; +2 max industries.
why: A military-restricted colony with no luxuries is orderly but joyless.

name: Ecumenopolis
effects: +2 max industries, +40% accessibility, income x1.5, ground defense x2, fleet size +50%, hazard -50%.
why: A planet-wide city with scheduled weather and strong defenses.

name: Faction Capital
effects: Stability +3; unlocks capital buildings; losing it gives -7 stability to all player colonies.
why: Seat of government, a prestige address; stability is already counted.

name: Coronal Hypershunt
effects: Growth -50 flat, Luddic Church immigrants (LCAttractorLow). Tooltip: max colony size 2, no extra structures for lack of living space.
why: Very limited living space on a megastructure.

name: Nidavelir Complex
effects: Adds the Nidavelir Complex industry and links the megastructure. No stat changes.
why: Industrial megastructure only.

name: Hostile Lifeforms
effects: Only +25% hazard (vanilla BaseHazardCondition).
why: Hazard is counted; dangerous fauna also threatens people.

name: Starkeep Bastion
effects: Only for Sephira Conclave owners: +30% ship quality, ground defense x1.5. With S-TechPad: tariff x0.85.
why: Strong orbital defenses (only under Sephira Conclave).

name: Sigma Irradiated
effects: Only +750% hazard (vanilla BaseHazardCondition).
why: Huge hazard, but hazard is already counted.

name: Cottage Industry
effects: Empty apply and unapply: does nothing.
why: No effect.

name: Darkness
effects: Only +50% hazard.
why: Hazard is already counted.

name: Unmotivated Cadets
effects: Military base marine production -size (-size-1 with an Industrial Planning admin).
why: Military production only.

name: Dangerous Sealife
effects: +50% hazard; Aquaculture food -3. No wildlife effect despite the name (the description is about ocean pH).
why: Hazard is counted; the rest is economic.

name: Extreme Weather
effects: Only +25% hazard.
why: Hazard is already counted.

name: Headquarters
effects: Stability +2 (ConditionData.STABILITY_HEADQUARTERS). Nothing else in this class.
why: Stability only.

name: Inimical Biosphere
effects: +25% hazard; Luddic Church immigrants (LCAttractorLow).
why: Hazard is already counted.

name: Irradiated
effects: Only +50% hazard.
why: Hazard is already counted.

name: Holy Forests
effects: Light Industry +1 output, only if owned by Luddic Church, Knights of Ludd, Ashen Keepers or Luddic Path.
why: Beautiful old-growth forests are a pleasant place to live.

name: Ancient Candi
effects: Does nothing (placeholder; description says unimplemented quest).
why: No effect.

name: Domain-era Meshugatron
effects: With working fuel production: fuel supply bonus, +3 volatiles demand, +2 max burn for non-hostile fleets in hyperspace.
why: Economic and fleet only.

name: Recivilized Minority
effects: Picks one industry at random (mining, refining, heavy/light industry, farming, aquaculture, fuel, military, commerce, tech-mining): that industry upkeep x0.5 and +1/+2 output, or for military +30% fleet size and ground defense x1.2, commerce income x1.2, tech-mining +50% finds. Growth +size, poor immigrants. Tooltip action to relocate people causes 1 unrest on both markets.
why: A forcibly reintegrated population carries some resentment.

name: Luddic Majority
effects: Only when habitable, with a rural industry and no heavy or military industry: stability +1, rural industries +1 output, growth 5 x size, Luddic immigrants (all x2 for player colonies after the Luddic expedition is defeated).
why: Close-knit faithful communities.

name: Mild Climate
effects: -25% hazard, growth +size, extra immigrants (LCAttractorHigh).
why: Already counted by the mod.

name: # Planetoid Mining
effects: Class is not in the jar (only an uncompiled .java$ file, and its apply is all commented out). The condition does nothing.
why: No effect.

name: Toteliac Habitat
effects: +50% hazard, cut by military buildings (patrol 20%, military 50%, command 80%, AoTD hexagon 100%). Those buildings also get food and luxury goods (hunting), limited by supply and fuel shortages.
why: Apex predators that eat people; hazard is counted separately.

name: Unlimited Production Chip
effects: Heavy industry +1 output (+ up to 6 - size more), fleet size +100%, +1 heavy and medium patrol, fleet quality +25%; pirates also get +2 max industries.
why: Military-industrial only.

name: Bultach Territory
effects: Only for the Bultach Coalition (orks): ground defense x2, fleet size x1.8.
why: Doubled ground defenses.

name: Defensive Dronesystem
effects: Launches up to 3 derelict drone fleets to guard the planet and system; +1 ship hull demand.
why: Automatic defenders over the colony.

name: Warscape
effects: Only with Tech-Mining: +10% hazard and +size ship hull output. Unapply is empty, so the effects stay after removal.
why: A battlefield surface littered with old war remains.

name: Aureate Siege
effects: Stability -10 (Golden Omega blockade). The Golden Omega fleets come from the Gan Eden quest scripts, which return every year with bigger escorts.
why: Omega machines roam the system; no settlement is safe.

name: Orbital Solar Array
effects: Suppresses Hot and Poor Light; Farming or Aquaculture +2 food.
why: Its living effect is the removed hazard, which is counted.

name: Proxy Patrols
effects: Player colonies of size 4+ friendly to the Dustkeepers: 1 proxy drone patrol (2 at size 6). Needs a spaceport.
why: Extra patrols over the colony.

name: Kassadari Claim
effects: Accessibility -100%, +50% hazard, growth -2 x size, poor immigrants.
why: Ongoing interference by the Kassadari Navy and cut-off trade.

name: Trustworthy Population
effects: Under Navarchy of Tania: stability +10, hazard -25%, fleet size x1.5, ground defense x1.75, removes the military market. Always removes Pather Cells and Luddic Majority.
why: Vetted, secretive population with strong defenses.

name: Lost Hope
effects: Fleet size x0.7, accessibility x0.65, income multiplier x(1 - 20) = x-19 (int bug; meant -20%). Removed if not Navarchy-owned.
why: Public outrage and hopelessness after the scandal.

name: Toxic Atmosphere
effects: Only +50% hazard.
why: Hazard is already counted.

name: Trade Center
effects: Stability +2 only.
why: A busy commercial hub is a desirable address.

name: Urbanized Polity
effects: Empty apply and unapply: does nothing in code.
why: Dense, lively hab-stacks; small values since the code is empty.

name: Orbital Mining Lazor
effects: +1 ore and rare ore output, +500 flat ground defense, +25% hazard.
why: A very large flat ground defense bonus.

name: Vulpoid Security Foxes
effects: Puts the colony's Pather Cells to sleep (no Pather attacks) when the workforce requirements are met.
why: Ideology-sniffing security cuts terror and crime but feels watched.

name: Vulpoid Servants
effects: With a Vulpoid population at least the colony size: stability +4, drug demand -1 (Population and Mining).
why: A Vulpoid in every home greatly raises quality of life.

name: HEPHAESTUS Cradle
effects: +50% ship production quality; Heavy Industry / Orbital Works marine demand +size (not removed on unapply).
why: Military-industrial only.

name: Volturnian Lobster Brutes
effects: Ground defense x3 (+200%). Has an immigration hook (+poor share, -size growth) but apply() never registers it, so growth is unchanged. No hazard (none in condition_gen_data).
why: Lobster brute guards triple ground defenses; nothing else takes effect.

name: Volturnian Lobster Brutes
effects: Same class as DE_Lobsters: ground defense x3 (+200%); the immigration penalty is never registered, so it does nothing.
why: Same as DE_Lobsters: tripled ground defenses.

name: Melting Ice
effects: Uses vanilla LCAttractorLow: only adds a Luddic Church share (10) to incoming immigrants. No hazard row, so no hazard change. Nothing about ice or climate.
why: Only changes which faction immigrants come from.

name: Edict: Forced Labour
effects: Building upkeep x0.4 (-60%). Stability -4, falling by 1 each month back to 0. Population growth -2 x colony size. Needs a Senate in the system and military presence on the planet.
why: A conscripted, forced-labour workforce makes tenants unhappy beyond the temporary stability hit.

name: Edict: Forced Relocation
effects: Stability -3 on all colonies in the system. This colony gets population growth +10 x size taken from the other colonies in the system (they get a matching penalty). Stays until the transfer is done.
why: People are moved by force; tenants dislike it.

name: Crossbow of Ludd
effects: Only when the market is owned by the Luddic Path: fleet size x1.7 and ground defense +300 flat; for 90 days after a donation, ground defense x5 more. Otherwise no effect (icon hidden).
why: A heavily defended militant Pather stronghold: well guarded but oppressive.

name: Benefactors
effects: IAIIC crisis base: fleet size up by external faction contributions, fleet contribution and market upkeep multiplied by (1 + escalation level). Economic and military only.
why: Fleet size and upkeep only.

name: Pre-Collapse Cryosanctum
effects: Max industries -1. On a colonized market it adds a Cryosanctum industry (disrupted for 180 days); the condition removes itself if that industry is later removed. History of organ harvesting in the description.
why: An old organ-harvesting vault under the colony is unsettling; the rest is economic.

name: Chemical Crystals
effects: Light Industry +1 luxury goods. Nothing else.
why: Crystal formations are a small local attraction; effect is mostly economic.

name: Psychoactive Fungus
effects: Stability -3. Drug demand of Population and Mining set to 0. Light Industry +2 drugs if the market is a free port. Description: violent illegal sellers.
why: Local drug fungus: tenants enjoy it, but the dealers bring violence.

name: Extinctive Virus
effects: Every industry's output of every commodity is cut by half (re-applied every 0.5 days). No hazard or stability change in code. Description: synthetic virus killing all organic life, outdoor work only in full protection.
why: A deadly synthetic virus outside; living there is grim even though the code only halves production.

name: Hyper-Ecumenopolis
effects: Size 15 stage (AscensionStage): +3 max industries, +60% accessibility, income x2, ground defense x3, fleet size +100%, hazard -75%, ship quality +25%. Orbital ring.
why: The top colony stage: very accessible, rich and heavily defended.

name: Followers of Ludd
effects: Stability +1, accessibility +5%, +1 production for all industries (all doubled with Luddic Majority). Stability -2 per colony item used, -3 per AI core in industries, extra penalty if an AI core is admin.
why: A faithful community with a small trade bonus.

name: Nutritious Wildlife
effects: Population food demand -3. Artisanal Farming output x1.2.
why: Edible local wildlife makes good food easy to get.

name: Relic AM Refinery Monopoly
effects: Fuel output of all industries x1.8. Nothing else.
why: Fuel production only.

name: System Bounty
effects: apply/unapply are empty. Only shows the system bounty intel in the tooltip.
why: No market effect; only a tooltip for the bounty intel.

name: Smuggling
effects: Marked unused in code: apply is empty. The description's stability penalty is never applied.
why: The class does nothing.

name: Free Port
effects: Stability -1 rising to -3, accessibility +5% rising to +25%, growth +3 rising to +10 (over 365 days). Immigrants include pirates, poor and independents. All goods legal, no transponder needed, smuggling income, more mercenary officers. Removed without a spaceport.
why: Free trade and loose rules: lively and accessible, but more questionable people and crime.

name: The Gulf Restriction
effects: apply/unapply are empty. Tooltip says no measurable effect has been established.
why: Flavor only.

name: Habitable
effects: Hazard -25% (gen data). Growth +(size-1). Adds a Luddic Church immigrant share (LCAttractorMedium). The mod already counts this condition.
why: Already counted by the mod.

name: Hostile Activity
effects: Stability -1 and accessibility -10%. Comes from the hostile activity event (hostile fleets operating in the system).
why: Hostile fleets around the system make it a little less safe and accessible.

name: Byzantine Vineyards
effects: ResourceDepositsCondition mapped to ii_wine with modifier +1 (IIModPlugin): adds wine output to the matching industry. No hazard.
why: Fine local vineyards make the place more pleasant and desirable.

name: Sigma Distorted
effects: BaseHazardCondition: hazard +175% only.
why: Hazard only, already counted.

name: Existing Infrastructure
effects: +1 max industry while the colony is exactly size 3. Nothing else.
why: Industry slot only.

name: Panopticon Monitoring
effects: The condition class itself does nothing (code commented out). It is a marker added by IX Panopticon Node/Core structures, which give ground defense, stability, suppress pirate activity and block the black market; rules text describes oppressive surveillance.
why: Total surveillance: safer, but people feel watched.

name: Show of Force
effects: Stability +1 and accessibility +10% (+2 and +15% with the Alpha core). Tooltip claims growth +size, but the immigration modifier is never registered, so no growth bonus.
why: A deterrent planetkiller site boosts confidence and trade.

name: Growing Lobster Population
effects: Only a 365-day timer that runs while a lobster bioforge is installed. No stat changes.
why: Timer only.

name: Low Gravity
effects: Hazard +25% (gen data) and accessibility +10%.
why: Easier launches give a small accessibility bonus.

name: Magellan City-Warrens
effects: Ground defense x4 for Magellan factions, x2 for others. Stability +1 for Magellan factions, -2 for others. Underground city maze.
why: Fortified underground warrens: very defensible, but cramped living.

name: Rebellion
effects: Stability reduced by the rebellion event's penalty (variable). Description: ongoing armed rebellion, prices of marines, weapons and supplies up.
why: An armed rebellion on the planet: violence and fear.

name: Tribute
effects: Income -15% (nex_tributeIncomePenalty). Growth x0.5 below size 5 and x0 (no growth) at size 5+, imposed by a foreign faction.
why: Living under a foreign tribute that caps the colony's growth.

name: Frontier Reinforcement Center
effects: Accessibility -40% on this market (comms congestion). Friendly markets in the system get +10% accessibility (+10% more after a raid on it is defeated). Spawns drone escorts for trade fleets and patrols.
why: Drone escorts guard local shipping, but the core clogs traffic.

name: Hyperspace Bipartisan
effects: Accessibility +50%. Hazard +50% depending on whether hyperspace clouds cover the planet. Ground defense x1.1 and +50. Mining +3 volatiles. Slipstream detection +7 ly (player, with the event stage). Links the planet to hyperspace with a jump point.
why: A hyperspace rift: great access, but storm clouds over the planet.

name: Meson Field
effects: Unfinished: apply only reaches spawnTerrain, which throws Kotlin NotImplementedError; unapply also throws. No stat changes. Not in condition_gen_data and hidden in the codex.
why: Unfinished stub with no effect.

name: Hellspawn
effects: Player-owned markets only: stability reduced by HellSpawnManager.getStabPenalty() (custom start penalty, value not visible). Hidden on other markets.
why: A stability penalty from a custom start; nothing else.

name: Outpost
effects: Stability +2 (ConditionData.STABILITY_OUTPOST).
why: Stability only.

name: Piracy Respite
effects: In the current mode apply does nothing to the market; pirates avoid the player's trade fleets, so shipping disruptions are greatly reduced.
why: Pirates leave local shipping alone for now.

name: Poor Light
effects: BaseHazardCondition: hazard +25% only.
why: Hazard only.

name: Pre Collapse Facility
effects: +1 to the research facility databank stat (lets a research facility make an extra databank each month).
why: Research only.

name: Ancient Fuel Production
effects: Mining +1 volatiles and Fuel Production +1 fuel.
why: Production only.

name: Rampant Military Core
effects: Forces an unremovable military Alpha-core administrator. Stability -1, fleet size +30%, +1 light, medium and heavy patrol.
why: An AI that will not give up control runs the colony; more patrols.

name: Extensive Ruins
effects: BaseHazardCondition with no hazard: no effect in this class (ruins only matter to tech mining elsewhere).
why: No effect on the colony.

name: Rural Polity
effects: apply and unapply are empty.
why: No effect.

name: Trade Disruption
effects: Temporary accessibility penalty from lost trade fleets (0.1 per market-size units lost, lasts 120 days) and reduced availability of some commodities.
why: Temporary trade losses.

name: Stealth Minefields
effects: Stability +1 (ConditionData.STABILITY_STEALTH_MINEFIELDS). Nothing else.
why: Stability only.

name: The Grim Phoenix
effects: Hegemony markets only (removes itself otherwise): stability -3, fleet size -25%, accessibility x0.9, ground defense x0.85.
why: A government scandal: distrust, unrest and weaker defenses.

name: Extreme Cold
effects: BaseHazardCondition: hazard +50% only.
why: Hazard only.

name: Extreme Heat
effects: BaseHazardCondition: hazard +50% only.
why: Hazard only.

name: Orbital Mine Shell
effects: BaseHazardCondition with no hazard: no stats. Added by the Volantian incursion raid, which also decivilizes the market; rules block all landing. The colony is effectively gone.
why: The planet is sealed by mines after decivilization; nobody can come or go.

name: Vulpoid Celebrities
effects: When requirements are met: colony income +10%, growth +5 x size (independent immigrants), +1 demand for domestic goods, luxury goods and drugs.
why: A booming entertainment scene draws people in.

name: Vulpoid Orbital Workers
effects: Needs a size 6+ Vulpoid population: accessibility +30%.
why: Much better orbital logistics.

name: Vulpoid Mine Laborers
effects: Mining +1 production, stability -2 (protests about Vulpoid safety).
why: Production and stability only.

name: Vulpoid Population
effects: Stability +0 to +4 by Vulpoid availability (population vs colony size). Player markets: growth up to +20 x size. Workforce capacity up to 4. Unapply does not remove the stability modifier.
why: Helpful pet Vulpoids in homes make life more comfortable and pleasant.

name: Vulpoid Shipbreakers
effects: Population & Infrastructure upkeep x0.75. NPC-only workforce.
why: Upkeep only.

name: Water-covered Surface
effects: Hazard +25% (gen data). Food via Aquaculture with modifier 0. Adds a Luddic Church immigrant share (10).
why: Hazard and production only.

name: GAIA Cradle
effects: Ship production quality +50% (CAULDRON Nanoforges). Does not call super.apply, so no hazard (and none listed).
why: Ship quality only.

name: Natural Freshwater Lake
effects: Vanilla ResourceDepositsCondition; BSFModPlugin maps it to +4 BSF_NeonCarp (koi) output at Aquaculture. No stability, hazard or other effect.
why: Clean drinkable lake with koi is a pleasant place to live; the code itself is only a production bonus.

name: Warm Waters
effects: Vanilla ResourceDepositsCondition; BSFModPlugin maps it to BSF_InstantNoodles at Light Industry (+1 modifier, base size-3). No stability, hazard or other effect.
why: Mild flavor of warm seas full of life; code is only a production bonus.

name: Titan Lobsters
effects: Extends BaseHazardCondition but has no condition_gen_data entry, so it applies nothing at all: no hazard, no stability, no spawns. Pure flavor despite the description of lobsters destroying arcologies.
why: Code does nothing, but the condition is giant monsters attacking arcologies, so a modest danger value.

name: Industrial Ruins
effects: BaseHazardCondition with hazard 0. On a colonized, non-neutral market it adds the IndEvo_Ruins industry (restorable into a Research Lab, Hull Deconstructor, Hull Forge or Rift Generator) and removes itself if that industry is gone. No stability, hazard or living-condition effect.
why: Only unlocks a special industry slot; purely economic.

name: Edict: Customs Control
effects: Senate edict (needs Senate in system, Megaport on this planet, 2+ own colonies in system). This market: +5% accessibility per other own colony in the system. Every other own colony in the system: -7% accessibility. Removing it early adds Recent Unrest (BaseEdict). Min runtime 186 days (155 with beta core Senate).
why: Accessibility up on this market makes it a slightly busier, more desirable hub.

name: Edict: Hard Deadlines
effects: Senate edict: +30% ship hull output and production budget from this colony, -20% ship production quality. Early removal adds Recent Unrest. Flavor mentions accidents and high turnover; the code has no stability or population effect.
why: Overworked shipyard staff with accidents; small mood penalty.

name: Edict: Mandated Overtime
effects: Senate edict: construction time of buildings on this planet halved (x0.5), output of all industries on this planet -50%. Flavor: 16 hour work days and conscripted labor. Early removal adds Recent Unrest.
why: Forced 16 hour days and labor conscription make tenants miserable.

name: Edict: Single-Child Policy
effects: Senate edict: freezes the population growth weight at the value for the current size, so the colony never grows. No stability effect while active; early removal adds Recent Unrest.
why: A state limit on children is an unpopular restriction of freedom; growth stopped.

name: #Engineered Plague
effects: Does nothing in game. Its row in IndEvo market_conditions.csv starts with '#', so the game treats it as a comment and never loads the condition; even if loaded it is a BaseHazardCondition with no hazard entry. The 'operating costs' in the text are not implemented.
why: Disabled (commented-out) condition with no effect.

name: Dockyards Donated
effects: IAIIC crisis deal: on Ailmar, combat fleet size x3; on player colonies, fleet size x0.8. Timed (about 365 days). Nothing else.
why: Fleet size only; no effect on daily life.

name: Investigations Underway
effects: IAIIC crisis: -2 stability and -20% accessibility; if the governing polity is not hostile to the IAIIC a further -25% accessibility (-45% total). Tooltip: trade ships stop-searched by unsanctioned patrols, security keys go missing. Timed.
why: Aggressive outside investigators searching ships and taking keys; less traffic and some harassment.

name: Arrow Pathers
effects: A Luddic Path sub-sect lives here: colony income x0.25, +1 max industries, new structures and upgrades start at 60% progress. No stability effect. Tooltip suggests removing them with a marine raid.
why: A resident Path sect is cooperative but still a fanatic presence; the mod does not count it under pather_cells.

name: Aristocratic Unrest
effects: Hegemony markets during the IAIIC crisis: stability minus the current unrest level (scales up to about 4, higher on Eventide and Chicomoztoc). Nothing else.
why: Stability-only effect, already counted.

name: Chaotic Structures
effects: Ground defense strength x2. Hazard 0 and no other effect; the description's claim that the maze hinders colony growth is not in the code.
why: Doubled ground defense makes it safe from invaders; a maze of half-built structures is a little less comfortable.

name: Crashed Terraforming Drone
effects: Hazard rating changes by (size-8)/10 with size clamped 3-6: -50% at size 3, -40% at 4, -30% at 5, -20% at 6. Nothing else.
why: Hazard-only effect (a reduction that shrinks as the colony grows), already counted.

name: Magnetic Crust
effects: +3000 flat ground defense; population growth -2 x size (size clamped 3-6, so -6 to -12); incoming immigrants include extra poor (+10 weight). Hazard 0.
why: Large ground defense bonus; lower growth makes it less sought after.

name: Space Farm
effects: Population & Infrastructure supplies food 3 + (size-3, max 3) and organics 3 + half of that, reapplied every half day. No stability, hazard or other effect.
why: Production only.

name: AI Legal
effects: Only when the colony admin is an AI core: +2 stability, colony income x1.3, +1 supply to every industry that has an AI core. Description is a copy of a capital text and does not match the effect.
why: Stability and income only.

name: CivSupplyContract
effects: Hidden (no icon). Adds a flat population growth bonus equal to the Civilian Supply Program weight; removes itself when the weight is 0.
why: Hidden growth bonus from a supply program; slightly more desirable.

name: Colony Development Program
effects: Wrapper that applies the chosen AoTD development plan (default 'standard'). Plans differ a lot: Bore City (underground, neutralizes hot/cold/extreme weather/meteor hazards, ground defense +200%, growth x0.75), Floating City (fuel-hungry thrusters, size cap), Centralized Core (upkeep -20%, ground defense x1.5), Distributed Network, Archeo-Site (size cap 3), Abyssal Frontier (no trade, size 4, no income), Persean Standardized, Hypershunt Quarters.
why: Effect depends entirely on the chosen plan; hazard and defense parts vary, so no flat value.

name: Pluto Mining Station
effects: Initializes the Pluto megastructure script for this planet and adds the pluto_station industry on a colonized non-neutral market. No stability, hazard or other direct effect.
why: Megastructure/industry hook only; economic.

name: Cracked Planet
effects: +25% hazard (condition_gen_data 0.25) and -2 ore and -2 transplutonic ore output at Mining.
why: Hazard and mining output only.

name: Terraforming Station
effects: +20% accessibility (applied always in the code, though the tooltip lists it under unlocked effects); after $scGargantiaRepaired, +2 food at a functional Aquaculture.
why: Better access plus a working terraforming station overhead; a nicer place.

name: Blockaded
effects: While a blockade fleet group is active in the system: accessibility minus the blockade penalty (default 60%, half that if the blockade is only evenly matched, 0 if it is weaker). Nothing else.
why: Hostile fleets harass shipping in the system; shortages and danger.

name: Decivilized
effects: BaseHazardCondition: +25% hazard only. In vanilla it marks a collapsed world with no ruling polity (bandits, looters, unknown population); usually it sits on uncolonized planets.
why: Code is hazard only, but a world with no government and roaming looters is unsafe for property.

name: Dissident Population
effects: -1 stability (ConditionData.STABILITY_DISSIDENT). Demand for weapons and marines and crew supply are commented out.
why: Rebels and troublemakers, but also artists and free-thinkers; small mixed values.

name: Matcha Makers
effects: Matcha resource deposit: +1 dpl_matcha at Farming (or any farming-tagged industry), base 0. BaseHazardCondition with no hazard.
why: Tea-loving community that shares its matcha; a small mood bonus.

name: Motivated Cadets
effects: Does nothing: apply() returns right after the base call, and its lookup table is keyed to 'dpl_unmotivated_cadets', not this id. No marines bonus, no defense bonus.
why: No effect in code.

name: Enigma III Economy
effects: Empty class: apply() and unapply() do nothing.
why: No effect.

name: Established Polity
effects: +10% accessibility (after beating the Persean League force, or as League development programs once you join).
why: Small accessibility gain; a recognized trading partner.

name: Filtered Air
effects: Suppresses pollution, extreme weather and toxic atmosphere if present, and removes pollution after 365 days. If none of those are present: -25% hazard (named Fine-Tuned Climate, or Edenic Climate with mild climate).
why: Engineered clean air and gentle weather; the mod may still count a suppressed pollution condition, so a small comfort bonus.

name: Hostile Terrain
effects: -20% accessibility (space hazards around the system make it hard to reach). Nothing else.
why: Harder to reach; slightly less desirable.

name: Standardized Atmosphere
effects: Empty: apply/unapply only call the base class, no tooltip effects.
why: No effect.

name: Eutrophicated Biosphere
effects: +50% hazard. Functional Farming also produces organics equal to half its food output and demands +3 heavy machinery.
why: Hazard and farming output only; the rotting algae is covered by the hazard.

name: Failed Cryosanctum
effects: Empty class; the source comment says it exists for flavor and does nothing.
why: No effect.

name: Logistics Complex
effects: If the spaceport is functional and has a Fullerene Spool: +30% accessibility (doubling the spool bonus). If a Planetary Shield is functional: extra ground defense multiplier equal to the shield's own bonus (doubles it, more if improved or alpha core).
why: Conditional accessibility and ground defense boosts.

name: Makeshift Solar Array
effects: Unless the planet has a vanilla Solar Array: suppresses Hot and Poor Light and gives +2 food at Farming or Aquaculture.
why: Its comfort effect comes through suppressed hazard conditions, already counted.

name: Subsurface Ecosystem
effects: ResourceDepositsCondition: -2 food at Aquaculture (and makes some ice planet types count as aquaculture planets).
why: Production only.

name: Water Ice Imports
effects: +1 food at Farming. Flavor: synthetic comets streak across the sky.
why: Production bonus plus a dazzling sky show.

name: Meteor Impacts
effects: +50% hazard (BaseHazardCondition, condition_gen_data 0.5). Nothing else.
why: Hazard-only effect, already counted.

name: Small Hydroponics Complex
effects: +3 food at Population & Infrastructure.
why: Production only.

name: # Star Volatile Collect Facility
effects: Does nothing in game: its market_conditions.csv row starts with '#' (a comment, never loaded) and the class is not compiled into the jar (only a stray .java$ file).
why: Disabled condition with no class.

name: Raiding
effects: Added while hostile raids are active in the system: stability -(raids+1) and accessibility -10% x (raids+1); one raid gives -2 stability and -20% accessibility. Removed when raids end.
why: Hostile raiding fleets in the system; the mod's pirate_activity does not cover Nexerelin raids.

name: Ultramagnetic Field
effects: +50% hazard, -25% accessibility, ground defense x1.3, refining upkeep x0.8, half of mining ore/rare ore turned into metals/transplutonics, and spawns a magnetic field terrain around the planet.
why: Electronics-killing field and storms (beyond hazard), harder to reach, but better ground defense.

name: Enslaved Population
effects: Only on Enigma-owned markets (otherwise unapplies itself): +3 to every industry output (tooltip wrongly says demand -3), fleet size +100%, +1 heavy and +1 medium patrol, -3 stability, +1 max industries.
why: Population held as forced labor by a rogue AI under harsh conditions; extreme.

name: Pirate Activity
effects: From a nearby pirate base: stability and accessibility minus the base's penalties (scale with base tier); removed when the base leaves the economy.
why: Already counted by the mod as pirate_activity.

name: Ancient Industries
effects: +1 heavy machinery, supplies, hand weapons and ships at a functional heavy industry; +1 domestic goods, and +1 luxury goods and drugs if legal, at a functional light industry.
why: Production only.

name: Bionic Plantlife
effects: Functional farming: +2 food, +1 organics demand. unapply() is empty, so the food bonus is never removed.
why: Production only.

name: Kinetic Launchsystem
effects: With a functional spaceport: +25% accessibility and +2 volatiles demand. Bug: the else branch calls unmodifyPercent on a flat modifier and unapply() is empty, so the +25% accessibility stays once it was applied.
why: Big accessibility boost makes it a well-connected place.

name: Regional Capital
effects: +2 stability (ConditionData.STABILITY_REGIONAL_CAPITAL). Nothing else.
why: Stability-only effect, already counted.

name: Gan Eden Sanctuary
effects: Clears its stability modifier and sets accessibility x0 (no access at all): the sealed habitat cannot trade with any other market.
why: Fully isolated sealed sanctuary: safe and self-contained, but cut off from all trade.

name: Pod Community
effects: Empty class (only a constructor): no effect.
why: No effect.

name: Lost Belief
effects: Only on Luddic Path markets (removes itself elsewhere): -5 stability, +25% hazard, accessibility x0.75, fleet size x0.75.
why: A faith crisis among the faithful; low morale beyond the stability hit.

name: Revitalized Confidence
effects: Only on Navarchy of Tania markets (removes itself elsewhere): accessibility x1.5, fleet size x1.25.
why: Big accessibility boost and a population freed from Luddic harassment.

name: Tectonic Activity
effects: +25% hazard (BaseHazardCondition, condition_gen_data 0.25). Nothing else.
why: Hazard-only effect, already counted.

name: Vulpoid Clerks
effects: Vulpoid workforce (needs size 6+ Vulpoid population, at least 1:1 with the colony, and workforce capacity): +1 max industries, colony income x0.8.
why: Economic only.

name: Active GAIA System
effects: +50% ship production quality only. BaseHazardCondition with no hazard entry; the terraforming agents in the text have no coded effect.
why: Code is production only; active terraforming agents keep the biosphere healthy, so a small comfort bonus.
